meta.title: Testing & Engineering — Movara Portfolio
meta.description: FMEA, free body diagram analysis, material selection, and structural testing for the Movara transfer bench.

banner.heading: Validating the Design Through Rigorous Analysis
banner.lead: Every design decision was subjected to formal engineering analysis — from failure mode identification to structural load calculation and material property comparison.

fmea.heading: Failure Mode & Effects Analysis
fmea.intro: A Failure Mode and Effects Analysis (FMEA) was conducted to systematically identify potential failure modes in the Movara design, assess their severity, and determine risk priority numbers (RPN = Severity × Occurrence × Detectability). Higher RPN values drove additional design revisions.
fmea.note: Edit the rows array to match your actual FMEA. S = Severity (1–10), O = Occurrence (1–10), D = Detectability (1–10). RPN = S × O × D.

rows.effect: Loss of smooth lateral motion; user unable to transfer
rows.cause: Prolonged exposure to water and cleaning chemicals
rows.mitigation: Anodized aluminium rail with sealed bearing carriages; periodic lubrication protocol

rows.effect: Loss of rotational movement; user becomes stuck mid-rotation
rows.cause: Corrosion or debris ingress into bearing race
rows.mitigation: Sealed stainless steel bearing with rubber lip seal; rotation stop prevents overloading

rows.effect: Sudden loss of seat height; risk of fall
rows.cause: Material fatigue under repeated cyclic loading
rows.mitigation: Safety factor of 3× applied to all linkage pins; redundant locking collar on adjustment mechanism

rows.effect: Bench tips; user falls into tub
rows.cause: User weight applied outside centre of mass envelope
rows.mitigation: Stability analysis conducted; non-slip feet; wider stance geometry enforced by frame design

rows.effect: Sharp edges; skin laceration; loss of structural integrity
rows.cause: Drop impact or over-loading above rated capacity
rows.mitigation: HDPE selected for impact resistance; rated load label affixed; rounded edge profile

rows.effect: Unintended movement during use; fall risk
rows.cause: Inadequate clamping force in wet conditions
rows.mitigation: Positive-engagement pin lock with spring return; tested under wet load conditions

fbd.heading: Structural Load Analysis
fbd.intro: Free body diagrams were developed for the critical load-bearing components of the Movara bench. The analysis establishes the design load envelope and verifies that all structural members meet the minimum safety factor requirements under worst-case loading scenarios.

materials.heading: Choosing the Right Materials
materials.intro: Material selection was guided by a weighted decision matrix, balancing structural performance, corrosion resistance, weight, machinability, and cost across candidate materials for each major component group.
materials.note: Edit the matrix rows to reflect your actual material comparison. Scores are 1–5 per criterion.

components.name: Frame — Structural Members
components.rationale: 6061-T6 aluminium was selected for the frame due to its excellent strength-to-weight ratio, inherent corrosion resistance in wet environments, and compatibility with standard machining and extrusion processes. Its lower density compared to steel reduces the overall bench weight, improving portability.

components.name: Seat Surface
components.rationale: HDPE was selected for the seat surface for its excellent chemical resistance, impact toughness, and comfortable tactile properties. It is non-porous (hygenic in a wet environment), UV stable, and can be textured for grip without additional surface treatments.

components.name: Rail & Carriage System
components.rationale: Anodized aluminium rail with self-lubricating nylon carriages provides smooth, low-friction lateral movement while remaining resistant to water and chemical exposure. The combination minimises maintenance requirements and eliminates the need for external lubrication in normal use.
